href="https://www.espn.com/nhl/player/_/id/2562637">Mika Zibanejad</a> became the Rangers' career leader in power-play goals, and his three-goal performance tied the team record for most career hat tricks in New York's <a href="https://www.espn.com/nhl/game/_/gameId/401803106/rangers-flyers">6-3 victory</a> over the <a href="/nhl/team/_/name/phi/philadelphia-flyers">Philadelphia Flyers</a> on Saturday.</p><p>The 32-year-old Swede scored with a man advantage at 5:38 of the second period, giving him 117 power-play goals and moving him past <a href="https://www.espn.com/nhl/player/_/id/2016853">Camille Henry</a> and <a href="https://www.espn.com/nhl/player/_/id/5833">Chris Kreider</a>, who each had 116 for New York.</p><p>Zibanejad's first-period goal at 7:26 put the Rangers ahead to stay at 2-1, and he completed his scoring at 8:25 of the second, matching Bill Cook with nine career hat tricks with the Rangers.</p><p><a href="https://www.espn.com/nhl/player/_/id/3891952">Artemi Panarin</a> added two goals and an assist, and <a href="https://www.espn.com/nhl/player/_/id/4874733">Brennan Othmann</a> also scored for the Rangers, who snapped a five-game skid. The Rangers, whose last victory had come Jan. 2 against Florida, had lost eight of their past nine games. <a data-player-guid="edddea19-8c2d-f283-933b-d0f4193c80f0" href="https://www.espn.com/nhl/player/_/id/2590852/jt-miller">J.T. Sullivan was a two-time Stanley Cup winner in his 10-year tenure with the Penguins.
